title: Best Running Shoes UK
short: Road, racing and daily-trainer running shoes compared by weight, cushioning and energy return.
intro: The right running shoe depends heavily on what you actually run: easy daily miles, tempo sessions, or race day. This guide compares shoes lab-tested by RunRepeat, which measures weight, cushioning stack height and energy return rather than relying on impressions alone.

products.name: Adizero EVO SL
products.best_for: Versatile running across a range of distances
products.summary: RunRepeat's overall winner, lightweight with a breathable upper and exceptional energy return, versatile enough for various distances, though the midsole is narrow with minimal support.

guide.q: How many pairs of running shoes do I need?
guide.a: Most runners are well served by one comfortable daily trainer for the bulk of their miles. If you race or do regular tempo sessions, a second, lighter shoe with more energy return can help, but it isn't essential to get started.

It's a measure of how much of the energy you put into the ground the shoe gives back through the midsole foam, generally as a percentage. Higher energy return can make a shoe feel more propulsive, though comfort and fit matter just as much for everyday running.

guide.q: Do I need a stability shoe?
guide.a: Stability shoes add structure aimed at controlling overpronation (the foot rolling inward). If you've had related injuries or a gait analysis has recommended it, a stability shoe like the ASICS Gel Kayano here is worth trying; otherwise a neutral shoe suits most runners.

guide.q: How often should I replace running shoes?
guide.a: A common rule of thumb is every 300-500 miles, though this varies with your weight, running style and the shoe's cushioning. Watch for compressed, less responsive foam or visible wear on the outsole as signs it's time to replace them.
